newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen down 110-120 bcf in wkly AGA.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen down 110-120 bcf in wkly AGA.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to fall by 110-120 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said Thursday.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for a drawdown ranged widely from 70 bcf to 170 bcf for the week ended Dec 20.

"Degree-day-wise, there should be some good pulls in the Midcontinent and Texas because of the weather, but the Northeast should stay at a large surplus to last year," said one Texas-based trader, noting eastern temperatures last week were not extremely cold.
In last report, overall stocks fell by 53 bcf, less than many expected, and were just 89 bcf, or 3.7 percent, below year-ago. The four week average drawdown is 74 bcf.

While Producing and Consuming Region West inventories continued to significantly lag 1995 levels, stocks in the critical Consuming Region East fell in the last report by just 44 bcf, leaving them 128 bcf, or almost 10 percent, above year-ago levels.

For the same week last year, total inventories dropped by 133 bcf due to some protracted cold. A draw today in the expected range would narrow the overall gap to last year to about 70 bcf. In 1995, eastern storage fell by 77 bcf, while producing stocks dropped by 44 bcf and western stocks by 12 bcf.
